title: Hypercohomology of a sheaf Hom complex into K-injectives
statement: Let C be a small category with Grothendieck topology J, R a sheaf of commutative rings, and A its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume a derived category D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let I be any endofunctor of integer-indexed cochain complexes in A [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose objects I(M) are K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. There is an additive natural isomorphism, on the product of the opposite complex category and the complex category, between (L,M) ↦ H⁰(C,Q(Hom•(L,I(M)))) [def-pur-hom-complex] [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] and (L,M) ↦ Hom_K(A)(L,I(M)), where K(A) is the homotopy category. The maps on the latter group are precomposition by L′ → L and postcomposition by I(M → M′). No resolution transformation, boundedness, or K-flatness of L is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 08JA (global assertion), using Lemmas 0A95 and 0A96 and Equation 0A8Z; source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08JA, /0A95, /0A96.

proof.text: Construct a natural map β from ordinary zeroth global cohomology of any complex to its zeroth hypercohomology. Whisker the right-derived unit by the homotopy quotient; transport across mapHomotopyCategoryFactors, quotientCompQhIso and homologyFunctorFactors. This map is an isomorphism on K-injective complexes by the right-derived unit computation [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

The ordinary global comparison [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-homotopy] is natural in both complexes. Precompose it by the product of the identity and I. For a quasi-isomorphism t:K→L, precomposition by q(t) on homotopy classes into I(M) is bijective: use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] on K and L, where it becomes precomposition by the invertible Qh(q(t)). The private helper bijective_precomp_quotient writes this argument explicitly.

Choose a K-flat quasi-isomorphism K→L using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The Hom-complex map to the K-flat source is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], hence hypercohomology inverts it. The ordinary global comparison and the preceding bijection show ordinary zeroth global cohomology also inverts this map. The Hom complex with K-flat source and target I(M) is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], so β is an isomorphism there. Its naturality square now forces β to be an isomorphism at (L,M). Assemble the componentwise isomorphisms, invert β, and compose with the ordinary global comparison. This proves the required natural isomorphism without choosing comparison data from an arbitrary witness.

proof_origin.place: Equation 0A8Z (sites-cohomology-equation-global-cohomology-hom-complex), degree zero; global computation in Lemma 08JA. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A8Z and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08JA.
proof_origin.description: T3: natural derived-unit comparison and two-out-of-three along a K-flat resolution; avoids common K-flat roofs and resolution-independence choices. The ordinary global computation is split into its own strictly simpler theorem.

from.place: The proof paragraph representing L by a K-flat complex and M by a K-injective complex: compute H⁰ of the global Hom complex as homotopy classes, before identifying them with derived morphisms.

theorem homComplex_hypercohomology
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))]
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ ⥤
      CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hI : ∀ M, (I.obj M).IsKInjective) :
    Nonempty (((𝟭 _).prod I ⋙ Functor.uncurry.obj (homComplexFunctor (R := R)) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology J R) ≅
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).op).prod
          (I ⋙ HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙
        Functor.uncurry.obj preadditiveCoyoneda)
